trust_decision.summary: Serverless upstream plugins must not forward the client's own message-framing headers (Transfer-Encoding / Content-Length) to the function backend after nginx has already de-chunked the body; decided in the shared generic-upstream access handler. At the pinned commit this protection is ALREADY present; the listed fix commit is the 3.18.0 release commit whose only source change is a version string.

landing_point.why: Shared access handler used by aws-lambda, azure-functions and openfunction; it copies client headers into the lua-resty-http request to the function URI.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Not applicable: the protection is already present at the pinned commit, so no route is left open for this advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The body and the remaining client headers must still be forwarded, and AWS SigV4 signs every forwarded header except connection, so dropping too many headers changes the signed set.

O9_family: HTTP request smuggling / framing-header desync (CWE-444) between gateway and serverless backend

O10_build.project_tests: t/plugin/aws-lambda.t (TEST 11 at t/plugin/aws-lambda.t:545-584 already covers chunked reframing), t/plugin/azure-functions.t, t/plugin/openfunction*.t

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Strip Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length before forwarding in generic-upstream access (already done at the pinned commit).

out_of_scope_notes: generic-upstream.lua:70-75 nils keys on the table from core.request.headers(ctx), which may be the per-request cached header table; not pursued.
Other hop-by-hop request headers (Connection, Upgrade, Keep-Alive) are still copied to the function request at generic-upstream.lua:70-104; not pursued.
